results.name: Skylar Breeze, a casual summer character scan
results.description: Skylar Breeze captures an easy, candid moment—a relaxed stance, hands on hips, half-turned smile, and the kind of posture that feels more real than posed. Dressed in a fitted light-blue summer dress with subtle texture detailing, white sneakers, and dark-framed glasses, she reads as contemporary and approachable without losing visual clarity in silhouette. The model balances realism with clean presentation, making it suitable for modern game environments, VR social spaces, crowd systems, or fashion/lifestyle visualization. Works especially well in daylight scenes and grounded urban or casual interior settings.

results.name: Lena Cross, a casual contemporary character scan
results.description: Lena Cross has the kind of grounded realism that makes a digital scene instantly feel inhabited. Standing in a relaxed neutral pose, she wears a black cropped camisole, frayed denim shorts, white sneakers, and dark-framed glasses—an everyday look that feels contemporary without becoming visually noisy. Her tied-back hair and slightly turned gaze give the model a candid, observational quality, like she’s paused mid-conversation or scanning a crowd for someone she recognizes. Designed for modern environments and real-time applications, she works well as a playable civilian, social-space avatar, NPC, or background character in urban, campus, retail, or lifestyle scenes.

results.name: The Three Graces
results.description:
The Three Graces (1813-1814), Antonio Canova (?) (1757-1822), Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek (Copenhagen, Denmark). Made with Memento Beta (now ReMake) from AutoDesk.

The Three Graces, celebrated in classical literature and art, were the daughters of Jupiter (or Zeus in Greek mythology), and companions to the Muses. Thalia (youth and beauty) is accompanied by Euphrosyne (mirth), and Aglaia (elegance).It was commissioned from Antonio Canova by John Russel, 6th Duke of Bedford, who visited the sculptor in his studio in Rome in 1814, and was captivated by the group of the Three Graces which Canova had carved for the Empress Josephine, the estranged wife of Napoleon Bonaparte. She had died in May of that year, and the Duke offered to buy the group from Canova, but Josephine's son claimed it, and that version is now in the Hermitage, St Petersburg.

For more updates, please follow @GeoffreyMarchal on Twitter.

results.name: The eagle finder
results.description:
The eagle finder (1890), Joseph Lambeaux (1852-1908). Dimensions: 236.5 x 144 x 114.5. Royal Museum of Fine Art of Belgium (Brussels, Belgium). Made with CapturingReality.

.He was part of a group of young artists, the "Van Beers clique", led by Jan van Beers. This group included the artists Piet Verhaert (1852–1908) and Alexander Struys (1852–1941). They were well known for their mischievous and eccentric behaviour, including walking around Antwerp dressed in historic costumes.
Other notable works include his Brabo fountain in Antwerp (1886), Robbing the Eagles Eyrie (1890), Drunkenness (1893), The Triumph of Woman, The Bitten Faun (which created a great stir at the Exposition Universelle at Liege in 1905), and The Human Passions, a colossal marble bas-relief, elaborated from a sketch exhibited in 1889. 

For more updates, please consider to follow me on Twitter at @GeoffreyMarchal.

results.name: Woman holding a hat
results.description:
Anthropomorphic whistle  in the shape of a standing woman holding, with her right arm a wide-brimmed hat with decorated edge. In her left hand, she holds a round fan with a cylindrical handle and a spiked rim, which she points downward. She wears a skirt, leaving her bust exposed, simple jewelry, and wears her long hair combed down the middle. A very interesting feature is the facial decoration, with designs on the cheeks achieved using the scarring or excoriation technique, which consists of making incisions in the skin that, when healed, leave marks or raised designs, especially if the skin is keloid. In some cases, to enhance the relief, pebbles or other objects were placed under the raised skin, like inlays.

 IDAEH Cultural Property No.  16.2.5.0918
 
www.fundacionrutamaya.org

Special thanks to the staff of La Ruta Maya Foundation for their hard work on this project.

3D model made using Artec Space Spider

results.description:

results.name: Magdeburg Characters - Blutappelsine
results.description:
The sculpture is part of the "Magdeburg Characters". Six figures that illustrate six individuals from Magdeburg and their eccentricities.

[Magdeburg City official Tourist Webpage for the Magdeburg Characters](https://www.magdeburg.de/index.php?ModID=7&FID=37.19279.1&object=tx%7C37.19279.1)

The "Blutappelsine" owed its name to the red cheeks it acquired from standing at the market in all weather conditions. The rosy cheeks of the chatty market woman were said to have shone as brightly as the citrus fruits. The "curves" of the "Blutappelsine" were also said to resemble those of oranges.

The model was scanned, retopologised, and cleaned by me. The model ist not fully optimized to a low poly version and is best used in renderings or the unreal engine with nanite. The appended file contains the remeshed version with the cleaned basecolor, the baked normal and a base roughness.
